title: Correspondence Standard: Counting the Successor Response Window by Occupancy Finding in Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases
content:
**Rule.** For the successor's notices on a Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases case, the window count is turned into calendar days by the counting convention. The convention follows the most recent occupancy inspection finding on the borrower's occupancy profile, held under Occupancy and Residency Certification.

- **Occupied by someone other than a borrower.** The household living there is given working days. The window count is counted in business days: each Monday to Friday after the mailing date counts as one day, and Saturdays and Sundays are skipped. The window is the calendar days from the mailing date to the last business day so counted.
- **Vacant.** The window count is counted in calendar days, and an end that falls on a Saturday or a Sunday moves to the following Monday.
- **Any other finding, or no inspection finding at all.** The window count is counted in calendar days with no move.

Federal holidays are counted like any other weekday.

**Which finding is most recent.** Where two occupancy inspection findings carry the same most recent date, a finding that the home is occupied by someone other than a borrower prevails over a finding that it is vacant, and a vacant finding prevails over any other finding.

Weekdays follow the ordinary calendar. For reference, 5 January 2026 fell on a Monday.

## Worked examples (hypothetical mailing on a Friday, window count of 10)

| Most recent finding | Counting | End day | Window |
|---|---|---|---|
| occupied by someone other than a borrower | 10 business days from the following Monday | the second Friday after mailing | 14 calendar days |
| vacant | 10 calendar days | lands on a Monday, so no move | 10 calendar days |
| other or none | 10 calendar days | the Monday 10 days later | 10 calendar days |

With a window count of 8 and a Friday mailing, the vacant convention ends on a Saturday. That end moves to the Monday, giving 10 calendar days.
